record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: Can one identify a nonempty class of 'natural' universal Turing machines or universal semimeasures, or even a single best such machine or semimeasure, that has favorable invariance properties strong enough to control the additive and multiplicative constants that otherwise pervade algorithmic information theory?

evidence.quote: h) Identification of “natural” Turing machines. In order to pin down the additive/multiplicative constants that plague most results in AIT, it would be highly desirable to identify a class of “natural” UTMs/USMs which have a variety of favorable properties. A more moderate approach may be to consider classes Ci of universal Turing machines (UTM) or universal semimeasures (USM) satisfying certain properties Pi and showing that the intersection ∩iCi is not empty. ... A grander vision is to find the single “best” UTM or USM [Müll06].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In algorithmic information theory, a universal Turing machine (UTM) U is a Turing machine such that for every Turing machine M there exists a constant c_M with K_U(x) ≤ K_M(x) + c_M for all finite binary strings x, where K_M(x) denotes the length of a shortest M-program that outputs x. A universal (lower-semicomputable) semimeasure (USM) is a function m on finite binary strings that is lower semicomputable, satisfies Σ_x m(x) ≤ 1, and dominates every lower-semicomputable semimeasure up to a multiplicative constant. The invariance theorem guarantees that quantities such as K_U and m are defined only up to additive (respectively multiplicative) constants that depend on the choice of U or m, and this freedom is responsible for many of the additive O(1) and multiplicative Θ(1) terms appearing throughout the theory.

Problem. Define a precise, nonempty class C of UTMs (or USMs) deserving to be called "natural" by means of a finite list of explicit invariance/robustness properties P_1, …, P_n (for instance, properties such as: optimality up to small constants relative to a wide class of reference machines; stability under standard simulations and prefix encodings; minimality of the constants in the invariance theorem when compared to specified machine families; canonicity with respect to a chosen universal model of computation), and prove:

(a) that the intersection ∩_i C_i of the classes determined by each property P_i is nonempty; and
(b) that every element of C provides quantitative control over the additive constants in K_U (or the multiplicative constants in m) appearing in standard results of algorithmic information theory, in the sense that for any two U, U' ∈ C the difference |K_U(x) − K_{U'}(x)| can be bounded by an explicit, small, computable constant uniformly in x.

Stronger form. Exhibit a single UTM U* (respectively USM m*) — a "best" universal machine — together with a precise optimality criterion which U* (resp. m*) provably satisfies, and which singles it out uniquely up to a controlled, explicitly bounded equivalence.

Either produce such a class C (and ideally such a U* or m*) with proofs of (a) and (b), or show that no such class with the required properties can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying a class of "natural" universal Turing machines or universal semimeasures, or a single best such machine, that would tame the additive/multiplicative constants of algorithmic information theory is a long-standing foundational open problem. Surveys of Kolmogorov complexity and AIT continue to highlight the dependence of K and of universal semimeasures on the choice of reference machine as an unresolved foundational issue, with no widely accepted canonical "natural" UTM or USM having been established.

status_evidence.title: Kolmogorov complexity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The invariance theorem... leaves finite strings unprotected against an additive constant determined by the arbitrary choice of universal Turing machine, and hence unstable and extremely sensitive to this choice.
status_evidence.claim: The dependence of Kolmogorov complexity on the chosen UTM is acknowledged as a foundational issue still without a canonical resolution.

status_evidence.title: How incomputable is Kolmogorov complexity? (Vitányi)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey discussing properties and limitations of Kolmogorov complexity and choice of reference universal machine.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys of AIT continue to treat the choice of reference universal machine as a parameter rather than a settled canonical object.
